## Execution strategy — **parallel-agent**

5 of the 6 gaps are **functionally independent** (different modules, different migrations, different endpoints). After a Foundation sub-PR serializes shared scaffolding, four agents work in parallel via `isolation: worktree`. Merge order stays serialized to avoid main-branch conflicts.

| Phase | Sub-PRs | Mode | Wall-clock |
|-------|---------|------|------------|
| 4.0 Foundation + ADRs | 1 | serialized (lead) | ~4h |
| 4.1–4.5 Core work | 5 | 4 parallel + 1 dependent | ~8h vs ~5 days serial |
| 4.6 Integration + Wave Completion | 1 | serialized (lead) | ~2h |

Total: ~14h wall-clock vs ~7 days serial (–85%).

### Sub-PR 4.5: Automated Quality Gate (GAP-012)

**Branch:** `wave/04-security-compliance/quality-gate` (from Sub-PR 4.0 after 4.1 merges)
**Mode:** Serialized (lead agent — depends on 4.1 moderation pipeline)
**Dependencies:** 4.0 + 4.1 (ModerationStatus reused as quality-gate failure mode)

**Scope:**
- `InstanceQualityReviewer` — 5 checks per Wave 3 ADR reference:
  1. WCAG contrast ratio ≥ 4.5:1 (jcolor.contrast math)
  2. CSS variables applied (no default values left)
  3. No broken asset URLs (HEAD-check sample)
  4. Visual regression ≤ 20% diff (hash-based, exact-diff deferred)
  5. Logo placement (bounding-box sanity)
- Integrate as a new `Step`: `QualityReviewStep` inserted between `ComposeThemeStep` and `PublishPackageStep`
- Report stored in `QualityReport` entity
- V39 migration
- Block DEPLOY when score < 70
- 3-layer docs `quality-gate/`
- Tests: each of 5 checks + threshold behaviour

## Anti-Patterns Rejected at Review

- ❌ Inline SVG render without sanitization
- ❌ Allow-any URL for AI provider callbacks (SSRF)
- ❌ Delete data without audit log entry
- ❌ Bypass moderation queue via flag
- ❌ Trust user-supplied prompt (already rejected in Wave 3 rules)

## Orchestration Protocol (lead agent perspective)

### 1. Foundation
Lead agent: create wave-04 plan + Sub-PR 4.0 foundation PR. Merge after CI green.

### 2. Spawn parallel agents
```
Agent 1 — worktree — Sub-PR 4.1 (GAP-018)
Agent 2 — worktree — Sub-PR 4.2 (GAP-041)
Agent 3 — worktree — Sub-PR 4.3 (GAP-042)
Agent 4 — worktree — Sub-PR 4.4 (GAP-073)
```

Each agent briefed with:
- Gap file path + acceptance criteria
- Target branch name (branching from 4.0)
- Shared scaffolding inventory (AuditLog, validators from 4.0)
- Testing + docs + checkstyle requirements
- Pattern constraints (State Pattern, Saga, etc.)
- Concrete file paths expected

Lead agent monitors, merges PRs sequentially as CI confirms green.

### 3. Serialized tail
- Sub-PR 4.5 (depends on 4.1)
- Sub-PR 4.6 (depends on all)

### 4. Risk mitigation
- Each agent uses a **unique migration number** pre-assigned (V36, V37, V38, V39 reserved)
- Shared files (pom.xml, application.yml, wave plan) updated only by lead — agents given instructions to add section markers, lead resolves
- Lead does rebases in worktrees if conflicts arise pre-merge

## Parallel-agent retrospective

**First use** of parallel worktree strategy at this repo. Wall-clock gain vs serial: real.

| Metric | Serial est. | Parallel actual |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| 4 middle sub-PRs (4.1-4.4) | ~5 days | ~20 min agent work + ~90 min human sequencing |
| Merge conflict events on main | 0 | 3 (application.yml — resolved via rebase each time) |
| CI failures attributable to agent error | 0 | 1 (CSRF test-profile secret not applied — trivial fix) |

**Lessons learned:**

- ✅ Pre-assigned migration versions (V36–V39) prevented DB-schema collisions — worked perfectly.
- ✅ Shared interfaces in foundation PR (Sub-PR 4.0) let 4.2 concrete impl come from agent without circular waits.
- ⚠️ `application.yml` was the main conflict point — 4 agents all added a distinct top-level key, but git merges treat co-located blocks as conflicts. Next wave: lead-agent owns `application.yml` and cherry-picks agent diffs.
- ⚠️ Agents occasionally wrote into the main repo working copy by mistake (all three — 4.1, 4.3, 4.4 — flagged this in their reports). They cleaned up, but risk is real. Next wave: stricter worktree-path prompts.
- ⚠️ Sub-PR 4.2 `DoubleSubmitCsrfTokenProvider` fail-loud guard broke @SpringBootTest suite until a test-scoped secret was added. Lesson: fail-loud guards need test-profile escape hatch.
